title: Redwood discovery - Opal Payments - latency & throughput
summary: Initial discovery on latency and throughput requirements for Opal Payments' fraud-detection inference. They are evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; p95 latency targets ~200-400ms for short prompts, burst concurrency up to 120 sessions, streaming required for partial results. Next steps: share benchmark spreadsheet, run 1-day token/sec test on Dedicated, security package and pricing proposal
topics: dedicated vs hosted vs private tradeoffs
action_items: Ava Martinez: Send benchmark spreadsheet + example prompt sets (due: 2026-08-03)
Jonah Patel: Schedule Dedicated pilot environment for token/sec run (due: 2026-08-05)
Liam Chen: Share sample request rate metrics and typical prompt lengths (due: 2026-08-02)
Redwood Solutions: Share security docs (SOC2 attestation, SAML SSO guide, KMS options) (due: 2026-08-04)
next_steps: Redwood to send benchmark spreadsheet and pricing tiers
Customer to confirm target p95 SLAs and average prompt distribution
Book Dedicated pilot window for 24-48h token/sec test
Follow-up call week of 2026-08-09 to review results
transcript:
00:00:00 - Ava Martinez: All right thanks everyone for joining, I'm Ava from Redwood, I'll hand it to Jonah to kick off with a quick runtime overview then we'll jump into your latency and throughput needs.
00:00:12 - Jonah Patel: Hey hi, yeah thanks Ava. Hi team Opal. Quick high level, Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private - we typically map these for customers who have different p95 and compliance needs. Today we'd love to understand your p95 targets, concurrency, and whether streaming is important.
00:00:28 - Liam Chen: Great thanks. So hi I'm Liam, CTO at Opal. We're building a real-time fraud detection flow that needs to give near-instant signals to our payment path. For short prompts (like 10-50 tokens) we wanna be in the 200-400ms p95 range. For longer contextual prompts (200-400 tokens) ok up to 800ms p95. Does that align with what Redwood can do?
00:00:49 - Jonah Patel: Yeah so for short prompts on our dedicated pools, p95 at 200-300ms is achievable depending on model and GPU profile. On hosted, we publish performance curves but there can be more variance - bursts can add queuing. For your 200-400 token prompts, 800ms p95 is reasonable on Dedicated with optimized kernels and batching disabled for latency-sensitive tails.
00:01:12 - Sofia Alvarez: Quick Q - are you talking about streaming responses or return whole output? We prefer streaming to start showing partial decisions to the UI.
00:01:18 - Ava Martinez: Streaming is supported across modes; it affects throughput and CPU/network overhead. For streaming with small token latency you sometimes trade batch efficiency. We can tune the runtime to prioritize low latency streaming at the cost of some tokens/sec.
00:01:33 - Markus Vogel: Our infra constraint - we have spikes during peak hours, concurrency can jump to ~120 simultaneous inference sessions, average QPS ~300 sustained with short 30-token prompts. We need graceful degradation rather than hard failures.
00:01:47 - Jonah Patel: Okay that's helpful. So two dimensions: sustained throughput and burst concurrency. For 120 concurrent streams with 30-token prompts, our Dedicated pools with autoscale + burst are designed for that; we'd recommend reserved capacity sized to your baseline (e.g., 200 QPS) and burst buffer for spikes. Exact GPU counts depend on model choice and quantization.
00:02:05 - Jules Carter: Any quick rule of thumb - tokens/sec per GPU?
00:02:08 - Jonah Patel: Roughly, a 8-bit quantized Llama2-13B variant on an A100 class node does about 350-600 tokens/sec depending on sequence length and beam/search settings. For shorter sequences and streaming overhead, the effective tokens/sec drops. We'll include model-by-model numbers in the spreadsheet.
00:02:24 - Liam Chen: Are those numbers for continuous batching or single-request latency mode?
00:02:28 - Jonah Patel: Those are measured under a mixed mode workload - continuous batching with low batch size to keep latency low. If you force single-request low-latency (no batching), tokens/sec is lower but p95 latency improves.
00:02:40 - Sofia Alvarez: Security question - can we run Private in our VPC? We have PCI constraints and need KMS-managed keys, SAML SSO, and audit logs retained for 365 days.
00:02:50 - Ava Martinez: Yes Private supports a customer-managed VPC deployment with KMS/HSM integration; we have an enterprise package that includes SOC2 report and extended audit retention. For Dedicated we also support VPC peering and customer-managed keys for payload encryption at rest.
00:03:05 - Markus Vogel: What about model custody - do you keep logs of prompts? We need strict controls, cannot have customer data used for model training.
00:03:12 - Ava Martinez: Under all enterprise contracts we provide options: no retention, ephemeral logging only, and explicit opt-in for retention with customer-controlled encryption keys. We don't use customer prompts to train models unless agreed.
00:03:22 - Jules Carter: Back to latency - what's the expected p95 jitter? We need <50ms jitter ideally at the 200-400ms p95 target.
00:03:31 - Jonah Patel: Jitter can be 30-100ms depending on network and model. With reserved Dedicated capacity colocated in your region and TCP keepalive tuning, we can push jitter to 20-40ms in practice. We'll run a regional benchmark to validate.
00:03:44 - Liam Chen: We also want to see streaming latency per token - for UI snappiness we need first-byte under 100ms and per-token emission under 25ms ideally. Possible?
00:03:53 - Jonah Patel: First-byte under 100ms is tough for long-context samplers but often achievable for short prompts on optimized models and pinned KV caches. Per-token 25ms is aggressive but possible with lower temperature greedy decoding and on high-throughput kernels. We'll include per-token timing in the POC test.
00:04:10 - Sofia Alvarez: For benchmarking, what do you need from us?
00:04:14 - Ava Martinez: Sample prompt sets with distribution (percentiles of token length), expected QPS and burst patterns, and any diversity in response lengths. Also if you want to replicate production auth patterns, share header sizes and any per-request pre/post-processing.
00:04:26 - Liam Chen: We'll export a week's traffic histogram and a small set of representative prompts.
00:04:30 - Jonah Patel: Great. On the POC scope - we recommend a 24-48 hour dedicated pilot with a minimal reserved pool sized to your baseline and a stress-run to simulate 3x bursts. We'll collect p50/p95/p99 latency, per-token emission times for streaming, and tokens/sec throughput.
00:04:45 - Markus Vogel: For Dedicated pilot, do you spin up in our cloud account or yours?
00:04:49 - Ava Martinez: Two options: we can run a sandbox in Redwood's dedicated environment configured for your profile, or we can deploy Dedicated in your cloud/account under contract (Private-style). The sandbox is faster to stand up; deployment in your account is preferred for final validation.
00:05:02 - Jules Carter: Pricing timing - we need estimated spend for Dedicated baseline.
00:05:06 - Ava Martinez: We'll share pricing bands in the spreadsheet: baseline reserved monthly commit and burst rates. For the POC we typically cover short setup credits; long-term pricing is in the proposal.
00:05:15 - Liam Chen: Any gotchas around streaming and batching interaction?
00:05:18 - Jonah Patel: Yes - streaming tends to reduce batchability because you flush tokens earlier; runtime uses continuous batching but will prefer latency policies which reduce batch window. We can tune `max_latency_ms` and `min_batch_size` parameters. Those are knob names in the API we can expose to your infra team.
00:05:34 - Sofia Alvarez: If we need stricter p95 than you can guarantee, is there a fallback path?
00:05:38 - Jonah Patel: We support fallback routing to lighter-weight models or local caches for deterministic paths. Also can hybridize - use local model for first-pass and Redwood for deeper analysis. That reduces net latency for critical paths.
00:05:49 - Liam Chen: Great. Anything else we should prep?
00:05:52 - Ava Martinez: If you can share the prompt sets and traffic histogram by Monday (2026-08-02), we'll provision a Dedicated sandbox and run a 24h token/sec + latency run by 2026-08-05 and sync the results on a call the week after.
00:06:05 - Jules Carter: Sounds good. Quick nit - SOC2 and SAML docs attached would be helpful.
00:06:09 - Ava Martinez: Yep we'll attach those.
00:06:12 - Liam Chen: Cool thanks, this was helpful.
00:06:15 - Ava Martinez: Thanks all. Recap: Redwood to send spreadsheet, security docs, and propose POC window; Opal to send prompt set and traffic histograms; follow-up week of 2026-08-09.
00:06:28 - [call ends]
